messages:
incidents-bot: PagerDuty alert: REDWOOD-ROUTER-01 high-error-rate -> routing failures reported from dedicated pool. P95 latency spikes, some 503s. auto-page #eng-oncall and #eng-runtime.
Alice (oncall): acked. I'm taking incident lead (IC).
Alice (oncall): quick summary from PD: sudden spike in router 5xxs for dedicated pool routes -> some traffic blackholed; autoscaler churned nodes earlier.
Mara (prod-support): multiple customer reports that chat responses time out ~11:10 PDT. Tickets linked: INC-4592, INC-4593.
Jamie (eng-runtime): looking at router logs now. initial hunch: fallback routing policy started sending to regional variants and created a routing loop. Also seeing weird capacity metrics from autoscaler.
Rishabh (sre): I see the autoscaler signal: dedicated_pool_available_slots dropped to negative values around 11:07, then HPA removed replicas around 11:09. suspect metric label mismatch from new metric exporter.
Alice (oncall): actions: 1) Halt autoscaling for dedicated pools (set manual replica count), 2) disable fallback policies to stop looping, 3) route health checks to known-good variant. Jamie/Rishabh please confirm.
Jamie (eng-runtime): on it. I'm running commands to pin replicas and flip routing flag.
Jamie (eng-runtime): ```
# scale dedicated pool to safe baseline
kubectl -n redwood scale deployment/dedicated-pool --replicas=8
# disable autoscaler
kubectl -n redwood patch hpa/dedicated-pool-hpa -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":8,"maxReplicas":8}}'
```
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: routing-config rollback -> v1.12.4 -> rollback initiated by Jamie.
Rishabh (sre): I'm toggling metric ingestion to isolate the bad signal. suspect metric name "pool_available" was renamed to "pool_free_slots" by recent agent but router code still reads old label -> misinterpretation. Temporarily disabling the new exporter.
Jamie (eng-runtime): disabled fallback policy in router.conf to stop cross-region bounce. ```
# routerctl set fallback_policy dedicated-pool none
routerctl: success
```
Mara (prod-support): customer-impact update: ~120 sessions timed out, 3 paying customers reported degraded latency. CS already contacted top-10 customers via email with apologetic note and workaround. Nate, can you confirm comms?
Nate (customer-success): confirmed. sent targeted message to affected accounts, offering priority support and post-incident follow-up.
Alice (oncall): good. Monitoring metrics. Is traffic recovering?
Jamie (eng-runtime): after scaling and disabling fallback, error rate dropped ~80% in 3 minutes. Some residual 503s from in-flight requests that hit blackholed nodes. Full recovery to normal by ~11:35 so far.
Rishabh (sre): root cause draft: metric exporter rename caused router/autoscaler to read wrong capacity signal. The autoscaler then scaled down replicas thinking there was spare capacity; with fewer replicas, router started losing connections -> router fallback rules rerouted to region variants which had fallbacks configured symmetrically -> created loop until we disabled fallback. Contributing factor: recent routing policy change removed a loop detection guard.
Alice (oncall): tagging incident severity: P1 while customers affected, lowering once stable. We need an immediate mitigation checklist so this doesn't reoccur.
Jamie (eng-runtime): temp mitigation applied: 1) pin baseline replicas for all dedicated pools, 2) add circuit-breaker to fallback policy to fail-open after 5 hops, 3) revert metric exporter change. I'll open PRs.
Rishabh (sre): also re-enabled synthetic health-checks to bypass pool metrics for routing decisions. added canary that checks real request success rate before triggering fallback.
Mara (prod-support): raising a support play doc for CS with exact wording & timeline.
Alice (oncall): handoff: I'll stay as IC until postmortem draft. Jamie take ownership of runtime fixes, Rishabh own autoscaler/metrics, Mara own customer comms. Nate coordinate follow-ups.
Jamie (eng-runtime): PRs: routing-config revert -> https://git.internal/redwood/routing/pulls/1983; metric-exporter revert -> https://git.internal/redwood/telemetry/pulls/452. QA passing in staging.
Rishabh (sre): add to runbook: never let autoscaler read unvetted metric names; require metric contract change with schema migration. Also add alert if available_slots < 0.
Alice (oncall): estimated customer impact window: 11:06 - 11:35 PDT. We'll publish a brief incident note after RCA.
Mara (prod-support): draft note ready, will wait for final RC.
incidents-bot: Incident REDWOOD-2026-03-15-01 created. Severity: P1 -> P2 (11:40 PDT). Postmortem assigned to Jamie + Rishabh.
Nate (customer-success): flagged affected customers for credits and follow-up call offers.
Alice (oncall): final checks: confirm autoscaler now reads correct metric, routing policy has loop guard re-enabled, and we have a recovery dashboard updated. Jamie/Rishabh confirm when complete.
Jamie (eng-runtime): loop guard re-enabled and routed config rolled to prod at 12:05 PDT. Verified via router logs.
Rishabh (sre): autoscaler metric mapping fixed; HPA restored with safe bounds and schema validation added to telemetry ingestion at 12:12 PDT.
Alice (oncall): closing incident thread in ~30m after postmortem draft. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Mara (prod-support): putting incident note in status page and CS playbook.
Alice (oncall): postmortem actions (short): ["enforce metric contract review", "add routing loop detector", "circuit-breaker to fallback policy", "default min-replicas baseline for dedicated pools", "customer follow-up process"]
